## Why

The agent's behavior should be checked again after any change to its instructions, its tools, or its model, by rerunning a set of evaluations (#53). Self-hosted Arize Phoenix is the chosen platform. It traces each turn, and it has datasets, experiments, and a side-by-side view of two runs. promptfoo was the earlier choice, but it's only a test runner, and Joe already knows it. Phoenix gives more, and it's new for Joe to learn, which is the point of this project. So try hard to make Phoenix work. promptfoo is the fallback, used only if nothing else works. This spike works out how Phoenix works with this app and writes it down. The build in #53 is planned later, from what the spike finds.

## Design

- [DEVELOPMENT.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT.md), section 5.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 3.1 (tests).
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 11.
- [Systems design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/systems.md), sections 5, 6, and 8.
- Phoenix docs: [Claude Agent SDK tracing (TypeScript)](https://arize.com/docs/phoenix/integrations/typescript/claude-agent-sdk), [TypeScript client](https://www.arize.com/docs/phoenix/sdk-api-reference/typescript/arizeai-phoenix-client).

## Open questions

None yet.

## Do

Joe isn't available while this runs, so don't stop to wait for answers. When a choice comes up, make it, and list it in the PR's decisions comment. When something can't be made to work, write down what was tried and what failed, then go on to the next item.

Answer each of these with working code, and write the answers into `research/agent-evaluations.md`. Lay it out like `research/agent-sdk-tool-scoping.md`: a note that it's research, not design, then Method, then Results.

- **Run Phoenix locally** as a Docker Compose profile in `compose.yaml`, listening only on `127.0.0.1`, with no sign-in. Use an exact image version. Say where its data is kept: its own volume, or a database in our Postgres.
- **Trace a coordinator turn** on the Agent SDK version the app uses (0.3.301). Add `@arizeai/phoenix-otel` and `@arizeai/openinference-instrumentation-claude-agent-sdk`, at exact versions. The SDK must be imported through the instrumented module, or no traces are made, so `runTurnWithSdk` in `src/agent/coordinator.ts` needs to change. Say whether each MCP tool call shows up with its inputs and result, and whether token counts do.
- **Run one evaluation case from start to finish** with `@arizeai/phoenix-client`: a dataset, a task, and scorers, run as an experiment. The task sends scripted user messages to the coordinator through the same code as `npm run chat` (`src/chat.ts`), for a new trip. Use a fresh user UUID each run, so memory starts empty. Set up any memory beforehand through the memory code (persistence design section 8.8), not SQL. Use the "user or trip memory" check from #48: "we never eat at chains" goes to user memory, and "skip I-35 this time" goes to trip memory.
- **Score it two ways.** One scorer is code that reads what was saved from the database. One is a model judge on `claude-haiku-5-5`, called with the Anthropic SDK and paid for with the Max plan's API credits. Its key is in `.env` as `JUDGE_API_KEY`. The name must not start with `ANTHROPIC_`. An `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` would make the coordinator bill API credits instead of the plan (`src/agent/claude-env.ts`). Check that the coordinator still runs on the plan token. The key is short-lived. If it's missing, or a call fails because it expired, write that down and go on without the judge. If the judge can't run on the Anthropic API for another reason, write down why. Don't switch to another provider, such as OpenRouter. Joe decides that, since he'd need credits there.
- **Run the case five times.** Say how much the results change from run to run. Using the token counts in the SDK's result message for each turn, and the judge's API usage, say how much one run takes.

Push the spike code to `spike/phoenix-evals`, a branch that never gets a PR, so merging the doc doesn't delete it. The doc links to it. The code doesn't need to pass `npm run check`.

## Done when

- `research/agent-evaluations.md` answers each Do item, with the output that shows it.
- On the spike branch, one command runs the case and the experiment shows up in Phoenix.

## Ends in

A PR with the research doc.

## Settled in

The PR. Propose each answer in the PR's decisions comment, and Joe agrees by approving the PR.

This spike works out how Phoenix fits this app and writes it down, so the build in #53 can be split into issues.
